The dataset for LM2 currently extends only to reference 1105; Torah 123 (reference 1123) has not yet been entered into the dataset. The source text (torah_123.txt) is a four-sentence practical-medical-ethical teaching in which Rebbe Nachman states: (1) mikveh immersion does not harm at all — any doctor who claims otherwise is no doctor; (2) immersion is positively good for bodily health because the body's sweat pores (נִקְבֵי הַזֵּעָה) must remain open, and their blockage causes weakness; (3) immersion in water opens those pores — with the caveat that very cold water contracts (מְטָרְשִׁי) them rather than opening them; and (4) the ascetic practices called 'הָאְרִיוַואנִי' are not harmful — whoever is harmed by them suffers only on account of pride (גַּדְלוּת). The word 'בְּחִינַת' does not appear at any point in the text. The structural device throughout is practical instruction and physical explanation — entirely eitza in character: mikveh → opens pores → bodily health; pride → harm from ascetic practices. There is no use of the equating formula 'X הוּא בְּחִינַת Y', 'X נִקְרָא Y', or any equivalent declaration that two concepts share the same essential nature. No bechina-based packages can be constructed from the empty bechina subgraph for this Torah.
